summary.text: An irregular galaxy has no distinct regular shape, with neither a nuclear bulge nor any trace of spiral arm structure, so it fits none of the regular Hubble sequence classes.
Irregulars are thought to make up about a quarter of all galaxies, and much of the Local Group is irregular, mostly dwarf irregulars.
Some were once spiral or elliptical galaxies deformed by an uneven outside gravitational force, and galaxy collisions can also form them.

facts.label: Share of galaxies
facts.value: About a quarter of all galaxies

facts.label: Typical size
facts.value: About one tenth the mass of the Milky Way

facts.label: Large exception
facts.value: UGC 6697 is an unusually large irregular

facts.label: Small Magellanic Cloud
facts.value: Still classed as irregular, type Im

items.prompt: Astronomers like irregular galaxies for studying how stars form. What do they offer that spiral galaxies do not?

options.label: Almost no gas, so star formation is easy to isolate
A view of star formation without the effects of density waves
Unusually old stars that never change
Perfectly regular arms to trace

items.explain: Their lack of structure means few density waves, so they are prime areas to study star formation without those effects.

items.prompt: A galaxy that once had neat spiral arms now looks shapeless. What could have done this?

options.label: It ran out of stars and shrank
Distortion by an uneven outside gravitational force
It slowed its rotation until the arms faded
Its arms were burned off by a black hole

items.explain: Some irregular galaxies were once spiral or elliptical but were deformed by an uneven external gravitational force.

items.prompt: Irregular galaxies are easily disturbed by running into larger galaxies or clouds between galaxies. Why?

options.label: They orbit too close to the Milky Way
Their small size leaves them prone to such effects
They have no stars at their centers
They move faster than other galaxies

items.explain: Irregulars are commonly small, about one tenth the mass of the Milky Way, so they are prone to environmental effects like collisions.

items.prompt: Why might dwarf irregular galaxies offer a window onto the earliest galaxies?

options.label: They are the most massive galaxies known
They contain no dark matter
They have low metal content and relatively high levels of gas
They are all older than any other galaxy

items.explain: They tend to have low metallicity and relatively high gas levels, and are thought to be similar to the earliest galaxies.

items.prompt: One irregular galaxy shows some structure but not enough to fit the Hubble sequence. Another shows no structure at all and is often shaped by collision. How are they labelled?

options.label: The first is Irr-II and the second is Irr-I
Both are labelled Irr-I
The first is Irr-I and the second is Irr-II
Both are labelled Irr-II

items.explain: An Irr-I galaxy has some structure, while an Irr-II galaxy shows none and is often shaped by collision or merger.

items.prompt: The Large Magellanic Cloud was once classed as irregular. What is it classified as now?

options.label: Still irregular, type Im
A barred Magellanic spiral, type SBm
A lenticular galaxy
A dwarf elliptical

items.explain: The Large Magellanic Cloud has been reclassified as type SBm, a barred Magellanic spiral, while the Small Magellanic Cloud remains irregular.
